who: Factory B builders, reviewers, CI jobs, and receiving implementation agents
what: A deterministic verifier for package manifest, hash, file-count, path, regular-file, and readable-member integrity
why: Every reusable Factory package needs a cheap independent byte/path integrity check before semantic verification or release review
when: After package creation, after transport/read-back, and before higher-level evidence or release decisions
where: Local Linux, GitHub Actions, or another environment with Python 3.11+
how: Read MANIFEST.json, validate required scalar types and declared rows, reject malformed/non-object rows, reject C0/DEL/C1 control-character and unpaired Unicode surrogate code points before filesystem encoding/resolution, reject colon-bearing, non-canonical, dot, repeated-slash, and Windows-drive paths, reject symlink directory roots and path components, validate ZIP directory entries and explicit Unix file-type metadata before member acceptance, enumerate directory contents fail-closed on scan errors, compare bytes/sizes/paths, optionally bind the manifest to an externally frozen SHA-256 trust anchor, and emit a machine-readable JSON receipt.
inputs: Factory package directory or ZIP containing MANIFEST.json; ZIP may use exactly one safe wrapper root
constraints: No extraction of ZIP content is required
approval_boundary: The verifier may report byte/path/readability integrity only; external release still requires the governing Release Contract and scoped approval
failure_modes: Unreadable directory enumeration that could hide unexpected members
Unsafe ZIP directory entries including symlink/traversal/absolute directory metadata
Explicit Unix ZIP special-file metadata including FIFO, character/block device, socket, symlink, or directory type on a non-directory-form member
C0/DEL/C1 control-character, unpaired Unicode surrogate, colon-bearing, dot-segment, repeated-slash, Windows-drive, traversal, or absolute paths
Malformed required manifest scalar types (schema_version, candidate, file_count, size)
Malformed or missing manifest, including non-object files[] rows
Symlink subject root, symlink path component, leaf symlink, resolved target outside the package root, or non-regular file
Corrupt or otherwise unreadable directory/ZIP member
recovery: Rebuild the package from the frozen source candidate and regenerate the manifest
Treat malformed/unreadable/corrupt or explicit non-regular ZIP members as FAIL evidence rather than allowing them to pass or an exception to escape
success_criteria: Corrupt ZIP member returns a machine-readable FAIL receipt
Malformed non-object MANIFEST files[] row returns FAIL without an uncaught exception
Directory parent-symlink and subject-root-symlink negative controls fail with zero verified files
Anchored mode rejects coordinated payload+manifest substitution against the frozen manifest hash
Malformed required scalar types fail closed instead of passing via Python bool/int equality or mere key presence
NUL/C0/DEL/C1 and non-canonical manifest paths fail closed without uncaught path exceptions
Unsafe ZIP directory entries fail closed while normal explicit directory entries remain supported
Unreadable directory enumeration emits FAIL evidence instead of silently hiding unexpected members
C0/DEL/C1 control-character, unpaired Unicode surrogate, and colon-bearing/Windows ADS-like paths fail closed before member lookup or filesystem resolution in directory and ZIP modes
Explicit Unix ZIP FIFO, character-device, block-device, socket, symlink, and directory-without-directory-form entries fail closed while regular-file and absent-type-bit entries remain compatible
known_limitations: Without an external expected MANIFEST.json SHA-256, PASS proves self-consistency only and cannot detect coordinated payload+manifest substitution
v1 supports the current Factory B MANIFEST.json shape
ZIP wrapper support is limited to exactly one safe top-level wrapper directory
ZIP entries without explicit Unix file-type bits are accepted for compatibility and remain governed by manifest/path/hash/size/readability checks
Concurrent filesystem mutation between path validation and byte read is not claimed to be hardened
It proves byte/path/readability consistency, not semantic quality, provenance truth, or release approval
provenance: F6.1 external MANIFEST SHA-256 trust-anchor patch
Gate B MAJOR-001 directory parent-symlink isolation patch
Supervisor probe PR #19 reproduced non-object MANIFEST row AttributeError on Ubuntu GitHub Actions; minimal loop guard patch then passed 14/14 artifact tests

Internal packet-only/process-isolated bounded review found fail-closed/path-enumeration gaps in v1.0.4; v1.0.5 patch candidate addresses only those supported findings. This is not TRUE independent approval.
Bounded same-17 cross-candidate matrix found ZIP colon/ADS and control-newline paths still PASS on PR #22; minimal general control-character and colon guards added

TRUE Clean Independent Review on frozen PR #22 packet returned PATCH_REQUIRED MAJOR-001 after reproducing U+007F DELETE and U+0085 C1 control paths as PASS; v1.0.6 minimally extends the control predicate to C0/DEL/C1 and adds matching-file directory+ZIP regression coverage.

Subsequent reviewer execution reproduced a new MAJOR fail-open where explicit Unix FIFO/character-device/block-device/socket and directory metadata on non-directory-form ZIP members could PASS; v1.0.7 adds explicit Unix ZIP member-type validation and focused compatibility regressions. Fresh clean re-review remains required.

Internal bounded pre-final saturation reproduced an uncaught UnicodeEncodeError for unpaired U+D800/U+DFFF manifest-path code points during DIRECTORY resolution. v1.0.8 rejects unpaired surrogate code points before member-path construction/resolution and adds DIRECTORY plus ZIP manifest-declared path regressions. This is internal supporting evidence, not independent approval.
